findings.assumption: Edits forced by the spec's own criteria count as within its Test changes, though it says "Kept unchanged".
findings.summary: Implementer gap 1 judged acceptable. [AC:spec-13-1] gains the text field in its expected list (spec-30-2 requires text; the test is stronger). [review-13-2] (:71) loses its --apply --rewrite half and the focused fixture option: that half pins removed behaviour and cannot pass once --rewrite exits 2 (spec-30-4); its listing assertions are unchanged. The spec's Test changes should have named both edits (class 1 for spec-13-1; the class 3 reason for the review-13-2 tail).

findings.assumption: The criterion is the named forms; the namesFolder anchoring is a kept item.
findings.summary: Probe: '../docs/features/<dated>/brief.md', `${root}/docs/features/<dated>/brief.md` and 'features/<dated>/brief.md' are not listed, because pathStart refuses any of [\w./-] before the path and namesDated only takes the name as the first path part. These spell the folder name, and join(__dirname, '../docs/features/...') and template paths are common in tests. Same as spec 13 for the full path, so not a regression. A fix: also accept a start after "}/" or "../" (keeps packages/app/... out). The gate or CI remains the check (ruling limit 6).

Implementer gap 2 judged acceptable: it is the f13-7 scan-cost fix the Keep list asks for (review-13-r2 said scan cost was never fixed). git grep -I -l -z -F on the folder basename is a superset of both patterns (each contains the basename), reads tracked files in the working tree, and exit 1 = no match is handled. One change from spec 13: a tracked binary that names the folder is no longer listed (probe assets/b.bin); an agent cannot path-edit a binary, so this is fine.

Implementer gap 3 judged acceptable: the spec cannot get the race by timing, and the test injects a full second apply at two fixed points (revalidation check, stage rename) via --import and syncBuiltinESMExports. It covers both kept branches (movedMeanwhile and the never-moved catch). If a Node change stopped the patch from firing, readFileSync(out) throws, so the test fails loudly rather than passing.

let output = null infers type null, so the editor flags output.plan / output.next. tsconfig.json includes only src and excludes tests, so neither pnpm typecheck nor vitest (no type check) sees it; the old file had the same pattern at :444. No effect on correctness or the gate; `let output: any = null` would quiet the editor.
movedMeanwhile names "another archive --apply" whenever the source is gone, also when a person deleted it by hand. It is still a no-change refusal; only the wording can mislead.
